turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I'm not here to be managed, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered. Why wasn't I?
But I'm not changing the grade.
"I'm not changing the grade." On what basis, Hale? And before you answer, tell me whether Owen was spoken to first, because that's what 4.1 requires.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"Keep going if you like." I'm writing down that you've given me no basis and no answer on whether Owen was heard first. Give me one reason that isn't a refusal, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
Okay. "The answer is no." I'll want that in an email from you today, with the reason attached, and I'm writing down that you didn't have one in this room.
